gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the meters' standby draw in the same units and turns it into charge lost while the cart is parked. Junctek's KG-F is rated in watts (0.4 W measuring module + 0.5 W display, which is about 17.6 mA at 51.2 V) and Victron's SmartShunt in milliamps (<1 mA). Over a 30-day layup that is about 12.7 Ah, or about 12% of a 105 Ah 48 V pack, against less than 0.72 Ah (under 0.7%).
standout_why: I compared against cartvoltage.com/best-lithium-battery-meter-golf-cart (cited) and cartvoltage.com/golf-cart-battery-meter-wrong-lithium (rank 2). The cited page already gives both raw figures, but in different units: Victron 'under 1mA' and Junctek 'about 0.4W' plus '0.5W'. It never converts them, never compares them and never turns them into pack drain. It also gives no standby figure for the Renogy 500A and no continuous or peak shunt rating for any meter. The cited page already covers Victron's 6.5 to 70 V limit and why that rules it out for 72 V carts. The rank-2 page gives no standby, shunt or accuracy figure for any meter. I could not open the other top results (Prosport, LiTime) because they returned HTTP 429 or DNS errors.
decides: This backs up ChatGPT's Victron SmartShunt pick for 36 V and 48 V carts that sit unused for weeks, because it loses under 1% of a 105 Ah pack a month. A Junctek KG-F with its display powered would lose about 12% a month. A cart stored over winter with a Junctek connected needs a disconnect or a screenless unit. For 72 V carts the Victron is out: its supply range tops out at 70 V and a 72 V LiFePO4 pack sits at 81.6 V when full. A 10 to 120 V monitor (Junctek or Renogy) is needed there, so the standby draw becomes the cost of choosing one.

findings.note: cartvoltage presents these as Junctek's own KG-F series figures, not specifically the KG140F's. Normalised at 51.2 V nominal: 0.9 W ÷ 51.2 V = 17.6 mA. × 720 h = 12.7 Ah/month, about 12% of a 105 Ah pack. Measuring module alone: 0.4 W ÷ 51.2 V = 7.8 mA, or 5.6 Ah/month (about 5.4%). About 17.6 times Victron's upper bound.
